L0: # django-apcore
L1: 
L2: Django integration for the [apcore](https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore) protocol — scan your existing Django REST APIs and serve them as MCP tools for AI agents.
L3: ## Overview
L4: 
L5: **django-apcore** bridges your existing Django REST Framework and django-ninja endpoints to the [apcore](https://github.com/aiperceivable/apcore) protocol, enabling them to be served as [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) (Model Context Protocol) tools that AI agents can discover and invoke.
L6: The core philosophy is **scan, don't rewrite**: instead of manually defining MCP tools alongside your API endpoints, django-apcore auto-scans your existing OpenAPI schemas (via drf-spectacular or django-ninja) and generates apcore module definitions. These modules are then served to AI agents through apcore-mcp.
L7: ## Key Features
L8: - **`DjangoApcore` unified entry point** — single class for all django-apcore functionality
L9: - **Auto-scan DRF endpoints** via drf-spectacular OpenAPI generation
L10: - **Auto-scan django-ninja endpoints** via built-in OpenAPI schema extraction
L11: - **Auto-resolve `$ref`** — Pydantic model schemas resolved from OpenAPI `$ref` references
L12: - **Annotation inference** — GET→readonly/cacheable, DELETE→destructive, PUT→idempotent
L13: - **Semantic module IDs** — action verbs from function names (`list`, `get`, `create`) instead of raw HTTP methods
L14: - **Three output formats** — YAML bindings, Python `@module` wrappers, or direct registry registration
L15: - **Output verification** — validate generated files for syntax and structure
L16: - **AI enhancement** — auto-enhance module metadata via local SLMs (Ollama/vLLM)
L17: - **Serve as MCP tools** via apcore-mcp (stdio / streamable-http / SSE transports)
L18: - **Generate a CLI** — `create_cli()` turns scanned routes into an apcore-cli Click CLI that proxies to your running server (`[cli]` extra)
L19: - **Output formatting** — Markdown or custom formatters for LLM-friendly results
L20: - **Pluggable middleware pipeline** — logging, tracing, metrics, and custom middleware
L21: - **YAML-based access control (ACL)** for fine-grained module permissions
L22: - **Django context factory** — maps `request.user` to apcore `Identity` automatically
L23: - **Embedded MCP server mode** — start MCP server alongside Django on startup
L24: - **Include/exclude endpoint filtering** with regex patterns
L25: - **Export to OpenAI tool format** for non-MCP integrations
L26: - **Tool Explorer** — browser-based UI for browsing schemas and testing tools interactively
L27: - **JWT authentication** — Bearer token auth on the MCP server
L28: ## How It Works
L29: ```
L30: Django Endpoints (DRF / django-ninja)
L31:         │
L32:         ▼
L33:    ┌─────────┐     ┌───────────────┐
L34:    │ Scanner  │────▶│ ScannedModule │  ← annotations auto-inferred
L35:    └─────────┘     └───────┬───────┘
L36:                            │
L37:               ┌────────────┼────────────┐
L38:               ▼            ▼            ▼
L39:      YAML bindings   Python @module   Registry
L40:               │            │            │  (direct)
L41:               └────────────┴────────────┘
L42:                            ▼
L43:                     ┌──────────┐
L44:                     │ Registry │
L45:                     └────┬─────┘
L46:                          ▼
L47:                     ┌──────────┐    ┌─────────────┐
L48:                     │ Executor │───▶│ Middlewares  │
L49:                     └────┬─────┘    │ ACL / Tracing│
L50:                          │         └─────────────┘
L51:                          ▼
L52:                     ┌───────────┐
L53:                     │ apcore-mcp│
L54:                     └────┬──────┘
L55:                          ▼
L56:                    MCP Transport
L57:               (stdio / HTTP / SSE)
L58:                          │
L59:                          ▼
L60:                     AI Agent
L61: ```
L62: ## Quick Start
L63: 
L64: ### 1. Install
L65: 
L66: ```bash
L67: pip install django-apcore[all]
L68: ```
L69: 
L70: ### 2. Add to Django settings
L71: 
L72: ```python
L73: INSTALLED_APPS = [
L74:     # ...
L75:     "django_apcore",
L76: ]
L77: 
L78: APCORE_MODULE_DIR = "apcore_modules/"
L79: ```
L80: 
L81: ### 3. Scan your endpoints
L82: 
L83: ```bash
L84: # Generate YAML bindings from django-ninja routes
L85: python manage.py apcore_scan --source ninja --output yaml
L86: 
L87: # Or register directly into the registry (no files)
L88: python manage.py apcore_scan --source ninja --output registry
L89: # Scan DRF endpoints
L90: python manage.py apcore_scan --source drf --output yaml
L91: 
L92: # Preview without writing
L93: python manage.py apcore_scan --source ninja --dry-run
L94: 
L95: # Filter with regex
L96: python manage.py apcore_scan --source drf --include "users.*" --exclude "admin.*"
L97: ```
L98: 
L99: ### 4. Serve as MCP tools
L100: 
L101: ```bash
L102: # Start MCP server (stdio, default)
L103: python manage.py apcore_serve
L104: 
L105: # HTTP transport with explorer UI
L106: python manage.py apcore_serve --transport streamable-http --port 9090 --explorer
L107: ```
L108: ## DjangoApcore — Unified Entry Point
L109: 
L110: `DjangoApcore` is the recommended way to use django-apcore. It provides a single class for all functionality, following the same pattern as `apcore.APCore` and `apcore_mcp.APCoreMCP`.
L111: 
L112: ```python
L113: from django_apcore import DjangoApcore
L114: 
L115: app = DjangoApcore()
L116: ```
L117: ### Register modules
L118: 
L119: ```python
L120: from apcore import ModuleAnnotations
L121: 
L122: @app.module(
L123:     id="analytics.task_stats",
L124:     tags=["analytics"],
L125:     annotations=ModuleAnnotations(readonly=True, cacheable=True),
L126: )
L127: def task_stats() -> dict:
L128:     """Return summary statistics about all tasks."""
L129:     return {"total": 42, "done": 10, "pending": 32}
L130: ```
L131: 
L132: ### Call modules from Django views
L133: 
L134: ```python
L135: from django.http import JsonResponse
L136: from django_apcore import DjangoApcore
L137: 
L138: app = DjangoApcore()

L227: # apcore-a2a (Python)
L228: ## What is apcore-a2a?
L229: 
L230: apcore-a2a is the 【105†A2A (Agent-to-Agent)†google.github.io】 protocol adapter for the 【106†apcore】 ecosystem.
L231: It solves a common problem: you've built AI capabilities with apcore modules, but you need them to talk to other AI agents over a standard protocol. apcore-a2a bridges that gap — it reads your existing module metadata (schemas, descriptions, examples) and automatically exposes them as a standards-compliant A2A server. No hand-written Agent Cards, no JSON-RPC boilerplate, no manual task lifecycle management.
